titulo: Connecting the Past and Understanding Experiences
titulo_es: Conectar el pasado y comprender experiencias
estandares: Narro hechos históricos y experiencias personales combinando distintos tiempos del pasado. Comparo épocas, figuras y acontecimientos con estructuras precisas.
competencias: Combinar pasado simple, progresivo y perfecto en una narración coherente; comparar hechos y personajes históricos; usar expresiones narrativas y conectores; manejar el registro de aula.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante escribe y presenta una narración en primera persona de un personaje histórico colombiano o mundial: qué estaba haciendo, qué había ocurrido antes y qué hizo después, comparando su época con la actual.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student writes and presents a first-person narration by a Colombian or world historical figure: what they were doing, what had happened before and what they did next, comparing their era with today.

lecciones.t: Pasado simple: verbos regulares e irregulares
lecciones.t_en: Simple past: regular and irregular verbs
lecciones.content_es:
Regulares

Terminación -ed con sus reglas: like → liked, study → studied, plan → planned. Tres pronunciaciones: /t/ (worked), /d/ (played), /ɪd/ (wanted).

Irregulares esenciales

  • go-went · come-came · see-saw · do-did · make-made
  • take-took · give-gave · get-got · find-found · think-thought
  • write-wrote · speak-spoke · break-broke · choose-chose
  • lead-led · build-built · win-won · fight-fought · rise-rose

Las tres columnas

Base, pasado simple y participio: write - wrote - written. El participio se usa en los tiempos perfectos y en la voz pasiva, no en el pasado simple.

Recordatorio

Con did / didn't el verbo vuelve a la base: Did he write it?, He didn't write it.
lecciones.content_en:
Regular verbs

The -ed ending with its rules: like → liked, study → studied, plan → planned. Three pronunciations: /t/ (worked), /d/ (played), /ɪd/ (wanted).

Essential irregulars

  • go-went · come-came · see-saw · do-did · make-made
  • take-took · give-gave · get-got · find-found · think-thought
  • write-wrote · speak-spoke · break-broke · choose-chose
  • lead-led · build-built · win-won · fight-fought · rise-rose

The three columns

Base, simple past and participle: write - wrote - written. The participle is used in perfect tenses and the passive voice, not in the simple past.

Reminder

With did / didn't the verb returns to its base: Did he write it?, He didn't write it.

lecciones.content_es:
Forma

was / were + verbo-ing: They were fighting for independence.

Usos

  • Acción en desarrollo en un momento del pasado: At 3 p.m. I was studying.
  • Escenario o contexto de una narración: The sun was setting and people were leaving the square.
  • Dos acciones simultáneas con while: While she was writing, he was reading.
  • Acción interrumpida: I was walking home when it started to rain.

La regla de la interrupción

La acción larga va en progresivo y la que la interrumpe en pasado simple. Normalmente while acompaña a la larga y when a la corta.

Ojo

Los verbos de estado no van en progresivo: I knew the answer, no I was knowing.
lecciones.content_en:
Form

was / were + verb-ing: They were fighting for independence.

Uses

  • An action in progress at a past moment: At 3 p.m. I was studying.
  • The background of a narration: The sun was setting and people were leaving the square.
  • Two simultaneous actions with while: While she was writing, he was reading.
  • An interrupted action: I was walking home when it started to rain.

The interruption rule

The long action goes in the progressive and the interrupting one in the simple past. Usually while goes with the long one and when with the short one.

Careful

State verbs do not take the progressive: I knew the answer, not I was knowing.

lecciones.t: Los tres pasados en una narración
lecciones.t_en: The three pasts in one narration
lecciones.content_es:
Cada uno con su papel

  • Pasado progresivo → el fondo, lo que estaba ocurriendo.
  • Pasado simple → los hechos, en su orden.
  • Pasado perfecto → lo que ya había pasado antes.

Ejemplo completo

The crowd was waiting in the square (fondo). Suddenly a messenger arrived (hecho). He had ridden for three days to bring the news (anterior).

Combinaciones útiles

  • When she arrived, they were eating. → ya estaban comiendo.
  • When she arrived, they ate. → comieron después.
  • When she arrived, they had eaten. → ya habían terminado.

Consejo de escritura

No abuses del pasado perfecto: úsalo solo cuando el orden no sea evidente por el contexto o por conectores como before y after.
lecciones.content_en:
Each one with its role

  • Past progressive → the background, what was going on.
  • Past simple → the events, in their order.
  • Past perfect → what had already happened before.

A full example

The crowd was waiting in the square (background). Suddenly a messenger arrived (event). He had ridden for three days to bring the news (earlier).

Useful combinations

  • When she arrived, they were eating. → they were already eating.
  • When she arrived, they ate. → they ate afterwards.
  • When she arrived, they had eaten. → they had already finished.

Writing advice

Do not overuse the past perfect: keep it for when the order is not obvious from the context or from connectors like before and after.

lecciones.t: Comparativos y superlativos en contexto histórico
lecciones.t_en: Comparatives and superlatives in historical contexts
lecciones.content_es:
Comparar épocas y figuras

  • The 19th century was more turbulent than the 18th.
  • Bolívar was one of the most influential leaders of the continent.
  • This battle was as decisive as the previous one.

Estructuras de precisión

  • one of the + superlativo + sustantivo plural: one of the greatest reforms
  • by far: by far the most important treaty
  • the + ordinal + superlativo: the second largest empire

Comparar cantidades

more / fewer con contables, more / less con incontables: fewer soldiers, less territory.

Cambio en el tiempo

Cities grew larger and larger. · The more trade increased, the faster cities expanded.
lecciones.content_en:
Comparing eras and figures

  • The 19th century was more turbulent than the 18th.
  • Bolívar was one of the most influential leaders of the continent.
  • This battle was as decisive as the previous one.

Precision structures

  • one of the + superlative + plural noun: one of the greatest reforms
  • by far: by far the most important treaty
  • the + ordinal + superlative: the second largest empire

Comparing quantities

more / fewer with countables, more / less with uncountables: fewer soldiers, less territory.

Change over time

Cities grew larger and larger. · The more trade increased, the faster cities expanded.

fichas.d_en: fewer with countables; less with uncountables.

lecciones.t: Hechos históricos de Colombia y del mundo
lecciones.t_en: Historical events in Colombia and the world
lecciones.content_es:
Vocabulario histórico

independence, revolution, colony, settlement (asentamiento), treaty (tratado), battle, uprising (levantamiento), reform, constitution, republic, empire, conquest, heritage, legacy (legado).

Hitos colombianos

the Battle of Boyacá (1819), the founding of Gran Colombia, the Constitution of 1991, the peace process.

Hitos mundiales

the French Revolution, World War II, the fall of the Berlin Wall, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

Verbos frecuentes

declare, establish, overthrow (derrocar), sign, defeat (derrotar), achieve (lograr), abolish, influence, found (fundar).

Ojo: found como verbo base significa fundar (found - founded), distinto del pasado de find.
lecciones.content_en:
Historical vocabulary

independence, revolution, colony, settlement, treaty, battle, uprising, reform, constitution, republic, empire, conquest, heritage, legacy.

Colombian milestones

the Battle of Boyacá (1819), the founding of Gran Colombia, the Constitution of 1991, the peace process.

World milestones

the French Revolution, World War II, the fall of the Berlin Wall, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

Frequent verbs

declare, establish, overthrow, sign, defeat, achieve, abolish, influence, found.

Careful: found as a base verb means to establish (found - founded), different from the past of find.

lecciones.content_es:
Abrir la narración

It all started when… · Back in 1810… · At that time… · One day…

Ordenar los hechos

first, then, after that, soon afterwards, later, meanwhile, eventually (finalmente, con el tiempo), in the end.

Crear tensión

Suddenly, everything changed. · All of a sudden, a shot was heard. · Just as they were leaving, someone shouted.

Cerrar

In the end… · As a result… · That is how… · Looking back, it marked the beginning of…

Ojo con eventually

eventually significa «finalmente, con el tiempo», no «eventualmente». Lo que en español es eventualmente se dice possibly u occasionally.
lecciones.content_en:
Opening the narration

It all started when… · Back in 1810… · At that time… · One day…

Ordering the events

first, then, after that, soon afterwards, later, meanwhile, eventually, in the end.

Building tension

Suddenly, everything changed. · All of a sudden, a shot was heard. · Just as they were leaving, someone shouted.

Closing

In the end… · As a result… · That is how… · Looking back, it marked the beginning of…

Careful with eventually

eventually means finally, in the end, after some time — it does not mean possibly. For that, use possibly or occasionally.

fichas.d_en: False friend for Spanish speakers: it means finally, in the end.

fichas.d: Justo cuando: introduce una coincidencia temporal.
fichas.d_en: At the exact moment when: introduces a coincidence in time.

fichas.d: Mientras tanto: acción paralela en la narración.
fichas.d_en: At the same time: a parallel action in the narration.

fichas.d_en: A classic formula to open a story.

lecciones.t: Saludos y comandos para la clase
lecciones.t_en: Greetings and commands for the class
lecciones.content_es:
Abrir y cerrar una sesión

Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. · Before we begin, any questions? · That's all for today. See you on Thursday.

Instrucciones académicas

Read the primary source. · Identify the author's purpose. · Take notes on the main events. · Discuss in groups and report back. · Support your claim with a quote. · Hand in your draft by Friday.

Interacción

  • Pedir aclaración: Could you clarify that? · Do you mean that…?
  • Pedir tiempo: Could you give us five more minutes?
  • Confirmar: So, if I understood correctly…

Recuerda

Todas las instrucciones van en imperativo. Para suavizar se agrega please o se usa Could you…?
lecciones.content_en:
Opening and closing a session

Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. · Before we begin, any questions? · That's all for today. See you on Thursday.

Academic instructions

Read the primary source. · Identify the author's purpose. · Take notes on the main events. · Discuss in groups and report back. · Support your claim with a quote. · Hand in your draft by Friday.

Interaction

  • Asking for clarification: Could you clarify that? · Do you mean that…?
  • Asking for time: Could you give us five more minutes?
  • Confirming: So, if I understood correctly…

Remember

All instructions use the imperative. To soften them, add please or use Could you…?

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Una narración histórica bien hecha usa tres pasados: el progresivo pinta el fondo, el simple cuenta los hechos y el perfecto retrocede a lo anterior. A eso se suman comparativos y superlativos para valorar épocas y figuras.

Puntos gramaticales

  • Con did/didn't el verbo vuelve a la base.
  • Acción larga en progresivo + acción que interrumpe en simple.
  • El pasado perfecto solo cuando el orden no es evidente.
  • one of the + superlativo + plural; by far refuerza el superlativo.
  • fewer con contables, less con incontables.

Vocabulario

Léxico histórico (treaty, uprising, legacy, overthrow), conectores narrativos y el falso amigo eventually.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

A well-built historical narration uses three pasts: the progressive paints the background, the simple tells the events and the perfect steps back to what came earlier. Comparatives and superlatives are added to assess eras and figures.

Grammar points

  • With did/didn't the verb returns to the base form.
  • Long action in the progressive + interrupting action in the simple.
  • The past perfect only when the order is not obvious.
  • one of the + superlative + plural; by far reinforces the superlative.
  • fewer with countables, less with uncountables.

Vocabulary

Historical vocabulary (treaty, uprising, legacy, overthrow), narrative connectors and the false friend eventually.
puntos_clave: Progresivo = fondo; simple = hechos; perfecto = lo anterior.
Progressive = background; simple = events; perfect = what came before.
one of the + superlativo va con sustantivo plural.
one of the + superlative takes a plural noun.
found (fundar) es distinto del pasado de find.
found (to establish) is different from the past of find.
